title: 15 brand tracking software options and how to choose the right one
summary: Compare 15 brand tracking software platforms, tools, and agencies on cadence, qualitative depth, and pricing, plus how to learn why brand metrics move.
body_markdown:
What is brand tracking software? +


Brand tracking software measures brand health over time. It surveys a defined audience at regular intervals and reports brand tracking metrics such as brand awareness and consideration, usually in a dashboard. Most tools also show how your brand performs against competitors. Options range from self-serve brand health tracking tools you run yourself to brand tracking companies that design and run the research for you.


What is the difference between brand tracking and brand monitoring? +


Brand tracking asks a fresh sample of your target audience the same core questions in every wave, so you can measure brand awareness and brand perception among the people you want to reach. Brand monitoring software follows online mentions on social media and review sites, and uses sentiment analysis to show how the conversation is changing. Monitoring helps you track brand mentions and share of voice as they happen. Tracking shows how your target audience sees your brand.


How much does brand tracking software cost? +


Prices vary widely. A DIY survey platform can cost less than $1 per response, while dedicated brand tracking tools often start at several thousand to tens of thousands of dollars a year, and some charge per market. A brand tracking agency usually prices each tracker as a custom project. Costs depend mostly on the number of markets, sample size, competitors tracked, and how often you run waves, so ask each vendor to price your actual setup.


How often should you run a brand tracking wave? +


It depends on how quickly your category moves and how often you make brand decisions. Quarterly waves are common. Monthly or always-on tracking suits brands with frequent marketing campaigns, because you see a shift soon after it starts. Whatever schedule you choose, keep it steady so your historical data stays comparable from one wave to the next.


Can AI-moderated interviews work alongside quarterly brand tracking surveys? +


Yes. The survey shows how much views have changed, and AI-moderated interviews with real consumers help explain why. When a wave shows a drop in one group, teams can interview people from that group soon after and bring the reasons to the same meeting as the numbers. The tracker stays as it is, so you keep your trend lines and add the context behind consumer behavior on top.


How do you find out why a brand metric moved? +


Start by checking data quality. If the question wording or the mix of people answering changed between waves, either one can move a metric on its own. Next, look at what happened in the market, such as a competitor’s price cut or a new campaign. To confirm the cause, talk to the people behind the change. Interviews with that group give you the reasons in their own words.
